The full axioms produce a classical class of laws. By the cascade the kernel $\mu_{0,t}$ is the kernel $\mu_{0,s}$ at a finer scale convolved with the step $\mu_{s,t}$. By covariance $\mu_{0,s}$ is a dilate of $\mu_{0,t}$. So each kernel is a shrunken copy of itself convolved with a law, which is the property the next definition names [\sscite{sato1999levy}, Def.~15.1, p.~90].

The transform $\widehat\mu$ and the image $A_*\mu$ are those of Section~\ref{subsec:cited-d}. The dilation of measures is $D_c := (cI)_*$ for $c > 0$, so that $\widehat{D_c\mu}(\omega) = \widehat\mu(c\omega)$. On the line it is written $T_c$, as in [\sscite{sato1999levy}]: $(T_c\mu)(B) = \mu(c^{-1}B)$ for Borel sets $B \subseteq \RR$. The same notation is used for a measure on $(0,\infty)$, such as a folded \Levy{} measure, since $x \mapsto cx$ maps $(0,\infty)$ onto itself. The dilation of functions $\mathcal{D}_\lambda$ is the one of (A8), mass-preserving. The ratio of a pyramid is $q > 1$, and $\ell := \log q$.

The logarithmic moments of the grid pyramids use one function of Sato's list [\sscite{sato1999levy}, Prop.~25.4(iii), p.~159], and the paper proves that it is submultiplicative, with the constant $2$. For $g(x) = \log(|x| \vee e)$ and $u, v \ge e$ one has $u + v \le uv$, so $|x + y| \vee e \le (|x| \vee e)(|y| \vee e)$. Hence $g(x + y) \le g(x) + g(y) \le 2g(x)g(y)$, both values being at least $1$.

A continuous function $\psi$ on $\RR^d$ is \emph{negative definite} when $e^{-t\psi}$ is positive definite for every $t > 0$. By [\sscite{schilling2012bernstein}, Thm.~13.14, p.~212], in the direction proved by Example~13.13 on the same page, a Bernstein function of $|\omega|^2$ is negative definite. The infinite divisibility of the law comes from subordination: Brownian motion run at the random time of a subordinator, an increasing \Levy{} process [\sscite{sato1999levy}, Thm.~30.1, pp.~197--198].

The pair $(A_t, \nu_t)$ is the \emph{\Levy{} data} of $\mu_t$, in the normalization of Section~\ref{subsec:cited-notation}. The \Levy{} measure is the rate of the jumps of each size and direction [\sscite{sato1999levy}, Thm.~8.1, pp.~37--38].

A law is \emph{self-decomposable} if, for every $0 < c < 1$, it is the law of $cX + Y$ with $X$ of that law and $Y$ independent of $X$ [\sscite{sato1999levy}, Def.~15.1, p.~90] (Definition~\ref{def:self-decomposable}). Shrinking the law by any factor and adding independent noise gives it back. These laws are the kernels of scale-space theory. On the line the kernels of the fully covariant families are exactly the symmetric self-decomposable laws \prog{V-line v0.1}{Thm.~7.3, p.~37}. In $\RR^d$, with rotation invariance, they are exactly the rotation-invariant self-decomposable laws \prog{iso v0.1}{Thm.~3.6, p.~13}, whose exponents are the $F(|\cdot|)$ with $F \in \mathcal{A}_d$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:cited-A35}(2)).
